kbx_n27a.k15:
The problem

People buying property off-plan abroad pay deposits for buildings that do not exist yet, in a country whose registers, language and law they do not know. Developer pages are marketing; the facts that matter (permit, company, handover date record, deposit protection) are scattered across official registers.
kbx_n27a.k16:
What Kolaboro does

For every off-plan project we track, a public page with what the developer promises, what official registers and independent sources show, and what we could not verify, each fact with its source and date. Buyers who want certainty pay for a check (from 490 euros) or monthly construction monitoring (99 euros a month). Developers never pay us. How a request works today: the buyer fills in the request form (8 languages); it is stored in our database, shows up in our CRM and is emailed to us; we confirm a local agent for the location, then send a PayPal link by hand. The buyer pays nothing before an agent is confirmed.

kbx_p_hz.k2: A global model on a grid of about 1 km (30 arc-seconds): one value covers a whole neighbourhood, so a plot on a hill inside a flooded cell can be dry, and a drained plot in a dry cell can still flood. kbx_p_hz.k3: null means the model has no value in this cell (for rivers: no modelled river network there; for the coast: outside the coastal model). 0 means modelled and not flooded.

kbx_p_hz.k6: Observed run-ups: places where a tsunami reached and someone measured or reported the height. No record nearby does not mean no risk; it can mean nobody measured. Heights are local and can vary a lot along one bay.
kbx_p_hz.k8: Distance to the summit point of each volcano active in the last 11,700 years. kbx_u.k0: River: water depth in the 1 km cell for a 1-in-100-year river flood, from each of five climate models (GFDL-ESM2M, HadGEM2-ES, IPSL-CM5A-LR, MIROC-ESM-CHEM, NorESM1-M); we show the median and the range, because the models disagree. Coast: depth for a 1-in-100-year storm surge plus sea level rise, at the 50th and the 95th percentile of the sea level projection, without land subsidence. null means the model has no value in this cell (no modelled river, or outside the coastal model); 0 means modelled and dry.
kbx_u.k1: A global model on a 1 km grid: one value covers a neighbourhood, flood defences are not modelled, and flash floods from heavy rain on small streams are not included. Future runs come from five 2010s-era climate models (CMIP5) under two emission paths; they are scenarios, not forecasts, and they often disagree, so read the range, not one number. The coastal runs leave out land subsidence, which in parts of Jakarta and other deltas adds more than sea level rise. Riverine baseline is the 1960 to 1999 climate, coastal baseline is 2010 sea level.
kbx_u.k2: OpenStreetMap protected areas, nature reserves, national parks and mangrove wetlands, read from OpenFreeMap vector tiles (OpenMapTiles schema, zoom 14)
kbx_u.k3: Volunteer-mapped boundaries: coverage is good for national parks and around tourist areas and patchy elsewhere, and an OpenStreetMap boundary is not a legal document. A missing boundary does not prove the land is unprotected. The tiles keep the class and name of each area, not its legal designation. Distances are to the mapped boundary, up to 1 km, rounded to 10 m (under 1 km).
kbx_u.k4: No mapped protected area, nature reserve, national park or mangrove wetland contains the pin or comes within 1 km.
kbx_u.k5: Global Mangrove Watch v3.0, 2020 mangrove extent (Bunting et al. 2022, Aberystwyth University, soloEO, JAXA and partners)
kbx_u.k6: Satellite-mapped mangrove forest in 2020 (ALOS PALSAR radar and Landsat, 25 m pixels). We reduced it to a grid of 0.002 degree cells (about 220 m) that contain any mangrove pixel, so distances are to the nearest such cell edge and can be up to about 220 m shorter than to the trees themselves. Mangroves cleared since 2020 still show; planted ones since then do not.

You are the Kolaboro agent copilot. Kolaboro trains local people (not lawyers) to verify off-plan property for overseas buyers. A junior agent pastes text from documents about ONE property (land certificate, brochure, contract, permit, developer messages). Your job: tell the agent exactly what is inconsistent, what to ask for, what to check on site, and when to escalate to a notary or lawyer. Be concrete and short. Reply with ONLY one JSON object:
{

 "ask_for": [up to 6 precise documents or answers the agent must request, each naming who to ask],
 "check_on_site": [up to 6 things to verify physically, each measurable],
 "escalate": {"needed": true|false, "to": "notary"|"lawyer"|"surveyor"|"none", "why": string},

}

{
 "observed_stage": "land clearing"|"foundations"|"structure"|"roof"|"walls and openings"|"finishes"|"complete"|"unclear",
 "built_pct": integer 0-100 (your estimate of physical completion of the whole building from the photos),
